entries.question: How is an edited comment marked, and what must the migration that adds the mark do?
entries.answer:
An edited comment is marked by a nullable timestamp field named `editedAt`. It stays null until the first edit, and each successful edit sets it to the time of that edit.

The migration that adds `editedAt` must not change existing rows. The release checklist also requires every new migration to have a one-line note saying how to undo it.

sources.cited_text:
# Release checklist

Before a change ships, run npx prisma migrate deploy against a fresh database. Every new migration needs a one line note saying how to undo it.

# Comment model fields

Read from app/src/prisma/schema.prisma.

The Comment model has the fields id, createdAt, updatedAt, body, articleId and authorId. It has no editedAt field and no deletedAt field today. Deleting a comment removes the row.

A comment has a nullable timestamp field named editedAt. It stays null until the first edit. Each successful edit sets it to the time of the edit. The migration that adds it must not change existing rows.
Deleting a comment sets a deletedAt timestamp and keeps the row. Comments with a deletedAt value are left out of comment lists. Only the comment author may delete a comment.

# Soft delete rule

Deleting a comment sets a deletedAt timestamp and keeps the row. Comments with a deletedAt value are left out of comment lists. Only the comment author may delete a comment.

# Comment ownership

Read from deleteComment in app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts.

A comment belongs to the user in its authorId field. Deleting a comment looks it up by id and by the current user id together. When the comment is not found, or belongs to someone else, the API returns 404 with an empty body. The 403 branch that follows in the code cannot be reached, because the lookup already filters by author.

# Edited marker

A comment has a nullable timestamp field named editedAt. It stays null until the first edit. Each successful edit sets it to the time of the edit. The migration that adds it must not change existing rows.

# Migrations

Read from app/src/prisma/ and app/package.json.

The database schema is the Prisma file app/src/prisma/schema.prisma. Migrations live in app/src/prisma/migrations, one folder per migration, named with a timestamp. The folder has four migrations today. They are applied with npx prisma migrate deploy, and the database address comes from the DATABASE_URL environment variable.

# JWT settings

Read from app/src/app/routes/auth/auth.ts and app/src/app/routes/auth/token.utils.ts.

Tokens are signed with HS256. The secret comes from the JWT_SECRET environment variable, and falls back to the string superSecret when it is not set. A token expires after 60 days.

# Article list limit

GET /api/articles accepts at most 50 articles per request. A limit above 50 is treated as 50. The default limit stays 10.

entries.question: How must an API error response be shaped, and which status codes does it use?
entries.answer:
New error responses must use the body the app already sends: an object with an `errors` key that maps a field name to a list of messages, for example `{"errors":{"body":["can't be blank"]}}`. There is no extra wrapper object.

The notes list these status codes:
- **422** for validation errors.
- **401** for a missing or bad token.
- **500** for any other error.

The notes don't say which status code a new error response should use.

The notes conflict on this.

The notes do not say which describes the current behavior. The policy describes the intended rule, and the schema note describes what the code does now. Comment lists should exclude soft-deleted comments under the policy, but the notes do not confirm that this is implemented.

entries.question: Who may delete a comment, and what HTTP status code and error body are returned when someone who is not the comment author tries to delete it, or when the comment does not exist?
entries.answer:
**Who may delete:** Only the comment's author. A comment belongs to the user in its `authorId` field. (The policy notes say this, and the code agrees.)

**Non-author or missing comment:** The API returns **404 with an empty body**. The code looks up the comment by both id and current user id, so a comment that doesn't exist and one owned by someone else produce the same result. The 403 branch that follows is unreachable.

The newer error format (`{"error":{"code":"...","message":"..."}}`) applies to new error responses and keeps the same status codes. The notes don't say whether this endpoint has moved to it, so the empty 404 body is the documented current behavior.
